title: dotnet: Runtime crash `script.is_null() is true` at `tie_user_managed_to_unmanaged`
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.4 and 4.4.1

### System information

Windows 10/11, Fedora 41

### Issue description

I'm making a multiplayer turn-based strategy game using C# for heavy lifting and gdscript for UI/rendering. As players build more units and more pathfinding is happening, eventually one player will crash with this error:
```
ERROR: FATAL: Condition "script.is_null()" is true.
   at: tie_user_managed_to_unmanaged (modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1411)
```
This always happens when the game is pathfinding from each "builder" to each potential "blueprint" it could work on (before executing a min cost max flow algo to assign them). This is ~100 builders to ~100-300 blueprints on a map with ~8000 tiles.

All of this pathfinding is performed within one frame.

### Steps to reproduce

I have not been able to pin down exactly what causes it, I'm thinking it's related to the volume of processing going on since it tends to happen when more builders/blueprints exist.

The error message suggests that an object I'm trying to pathfind against is somehow getting destroyed, but I have not been able to find anywhere that could happen in my code (nothing is ever explicitly freed, only destroyed through garbage collection and I keep multiple references to each object in different places).

It seems somewhat similar to #70449

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I'm sorry I haven't been able to make an MRP, I'm really not sure exactly what causes this bug.
